Surrender. Easy to say, harder to do. It’s a word
that makes most people feel uncomfortable. It
means relinquishing control and entrusting yourself
to someone else.
We have two choices. We will give ourselves fully
to this world, running after its pleasures and “bling”,
letting others dictate to us what is right and good
and fulfilling, and asking ourselves each morning
as we hurry off to work… is this really the abun-
dant life?
Consider the second option – we surrender our-
selves to Jesus. We believe God truly loves us

(Jn 3.16). That His intentions towards us are kind
and good (Eph 1.9), and that He plans to give us a
future and a hope (Jer 29.11). We were made for this.
Most Christians don’t purposely walk away from
God; rather, they drift away. We miss the abundant
life Jesus promised and simply settle for “good
enough”. We choose to hold tightly to our wants
and desires, our time and treasures, unwilling to
release it all to Christ not realizing by hording our
lives, we lose it all (Mt 10:38–39).
The choice is all yours. Our good and giving God is
raising up a new generation of men and women to
follow Him fully. Has God put His hand on your life
for “such a time as this”?

to illustrate how the condition of our hearts can potentially lead to a
life of influence, impact and purpose.
Observe the four different soils. How would you de-

Which soil best describes you right
now and why?
The heart described by the soil with thorns and weeds
is ultimately unfruitful. This heart struggles with two
issues: the cares of this world and the deceitfulness
of riches Lk 10.38–42; Heb 12.1–2.

Kingdom Vision
The movement you were part of on campus and the
vision you had for making a kingdom impact there were
vital. They helped you fulfill God’s purposes for you.
Where will you find that same environment next?
Plan
If you aim at nothing you’ll hit it every time. Unless you’re a trained
chef or just incredibly gifted, most people don’t walk into the kitch-
en and whip up a gourmet meal without a recipe. It doesn’t have
to be elaborate, but the plan should have simple, doable steps that
will help you begin to implement your God-given vision. What are
your first three steps to bring about this vision for God’s Kingdom?
The
Five
Things
Team
Without a compelling community,
few people can survive for long
on their own. Ecclesiastes 4 says,
“It’s better to have a partner than
go it alone. Share the work… and
if one falls down, the other helps.”
Who shares your heart, in that they,
too, are surrendered to Jesus and
have a vision for your industry or
neighborhood?
Ongoing Equipping
Just as teachers, pilots and doctors need continuing education, so
you will need ongoing equipping in order to make your best contri-
bution to the kingdom.
Coach
Proverbs stresses the importance of gaining wisdom from others.
We can never underestimate the blessing of another who has gone
before us and learned a thing or two along the way. A coach is just
that person: someone to answer your questions, help you when
you might be stuck, or encourage you when the going gets tough.
If there is someone already out there doing what you have a vision
for? Can you join them?
